page: Microsoft Azure D64as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 64 vCPUs derived from 32 dedicated physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. System memory totals 256.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage, requiring network-attached storage configurations, and operates without discrete GPUs.

Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, alongside AES and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded compute, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 22,176.0 placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances. Multi-core stress-ng tests (98,472.35) and PassMark CPU performance (75,314.24) consistently register in the top quartile, complemented by strong software compilation benchmarks (54,274.0 in Clang tests).

Memory throughput exhibits distinct behavioral tiers, yielding 4,862.58 GB/sec in cached small-block read testing, while large-block uncached sequential reads settle at an average 151.2 GB/sec and writes achieve a strong 108.16 GB/sec. Application testing reveals strong throughput for in-memory operations, including 86.52 million Redis SET operations per second and 45.73 GB/sec in static web serving. Natural language inference on smaller models scales well, reaching 3,572.84 prompt tokens per second on a 135M parameter model, though throughput moderates to average levels on 70B parameter models (16.53 prompt tokens per second).

With 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of RAM, the instance delivers high resource density for workloads demanding high parallel CPU throughput without requiring specialized accelerators. Common target deployments include large-scale web application serving, CI/CD compilation pipelines, relational or in-memory databases, and distributed ETL data processing.

The architecture includes AVX-512 vector acceleration (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic hardware primitives, while omitting local storage and GPU accelerators.
